Plotting latent mixture models

plotting.Rmd

Every fitted model and every auxiliary result has an autoplot() method built on ggplot2; plot() draws the same figure. The functions return ggplot objects, so they can be changed like any other ggplot. The examples use the simulated datasets of the package (?aces, ?wellbeing, ?substance, ?depression).

library(latentmixtures)
library(ggplot2)
data(aces)

# four classes of adverse childhood experiences
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
autoplot(m)                                   # item-response profiles

autoplot(m, labels = c("Low", "Maltreatment", "Household", "High")) +
  labs(title = "Four classes of childhood adversity", x = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
ggsave(f, autoplot(m), width = 7, height = 4)

All figures share one theme, lm_theme() (minimal, horizontal grid lines, legend at the bottom), and the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette, lm_palette(). Both can be used for your own figures:

ggplot(aces, aes(age, depress, colour = factor(female))) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.3, height = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = lm_palette(), labels = c("men", "women"), name = NULL) +
  lm_theme(base_size = 12, grid = "xy")
#> Warning: Removed 47 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).

Figures that need parameters, posteriors or growth factors call the Julia session in which the model was fitted; class sizes and the classification table use only the summary kept in the R object.

Latent class analysis

type = "profile" (the default) plots the probability of one category of every indicator by class, with the class sizes in the legend. With binary indicators the highest category is shown; with polytomous indicators every category gets a panel, or category picks one (a label, a number, "first" or "last"). error = "ci" adds Wald confidence intervals ("se": plus or minus one standard error).

autoplot(m, error = "ci")

autoplot(m, items = c("ace_violence", "ace_substance", "ace_mental"))   # a subset

autoplot(m, type = "bars")                       # stacked category probabilities

Class sizes and classification quality:

autoplot(m, type = "sizes")            # estimated proportions, modal-class counts

autoplot(m, type = "classification")   # average posterior by modal class (heat map)

autoplot(m, type = "posterior", threshold = 0.7)

Latent profile analysis

Profile plots show the class means with 95% confidence intervals by default (error = "se", "sd" for the within-profile standard deviation, or "none"). standardize = TRUE expresses means and bars in units of the model-implied overall standard deviation of each indicator, centred at its overall mean, which puts indicators on different scales (hours of sleep, a 0–16 stress score) side by side.

data(wellbeing)
p <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying")
autoplot(p)

autoplot(p, standardize = TRUE, error = "sd")

# models with within-profile covariances: correlation heat maps per profile
p_full <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 4, variances = "varying", covariances = "varying")
autoplot(p_full, type = "correlation")   # e.g. stress and life satisfaction: negative

Class enumeration

lm_fitplot() plots the information criteria against the number of classes, with the entropy in a second panel and the LMR / BLRT p-values (given as for lm_table()) above the points; the lowest value of each criterion is circled.

fits <- lapply(1:6, function(k) lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = k))
lm_fitplot(fits, lmr = lapply(fits, function(m) if (m$info$fit$K > 1) lmr(m)))

lm_fitplot(fits, criteria = "bic", entropy = FALSE)   # minimum at K = 4

lm_fitplot(fittable(fits))                   # from a data frame of fit statistics

autoplot(blrt(fits[[4]], reps = 100))        # bootstrap distribution of the LR statistic

Models with the same number of classes (e.g. measurement-invariance models across sex) are shown as a dot plot, one row per model:

full <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female)
part <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "ace_sex_abuse")
none <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, group = female, invariance = "none")
autoplot(compare_models(full, part, none))

Multigroup profiles get one panel per group (0 = men, 1 = women):

autoplot(part)

autoplot(part, type = "sizes")

autoplot(part, category = "all", group = 2)

Latent transition analysis 

data(substance)
t3 <- lta(substance, list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3)
autoplot(t3)                                 # transition matrices, one panel per transition

autoplot(t3, type = "prevalence")            # class proportions over the waves

autoplot(t3, type = "prevalence", geom = "area")

autoplot(t3, type = "profile")               # item profiles at every wave

With invariance = "none" the item profiles differ between the waves, and type = "profile" shows where.

Growth mixture models

type = "trajectories" draws the estimated mean trajectory of every class. With the data the model was fitted to, the observed class means at every occasion (posterior-probability-weighted means of the observed values) are added as points, and spaghetti individual trajectories, coloured by modal class, in the background. Parallel-process models get one panel per process.

data(depression)
g <- growth(depression, dep1:dep5, K = 4, model = "gmm", degree = 2)
autoplot(g)

autoplot(g, data = depression, spaghetti = 100, seed = 2)

pp <- growth(depression, K = 4, model = "gmm", processes = list(dep1:dep5, anx1:anx5))
autoplot(pp, data = depression)

Covariates and distal outcomes 

autoplot(r3step(m, aces, c(female, low_parent_edu), ref = 1))  # odds ratios, 95% CIs

autoplot(bch(m, aces, depress))              # class means of depressive symptoms

autoplot(dcat(m, aces, srh))                 # class-specific self-rated health

mo <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, covariates = c(female, low_parent_edu), ref = 1)
autoplot(mo, type = "regression")            # one-step covariate model
